purpose: Track narratives that attribute access degradation or blocking of foreign platforms to the foreign platform/provider itself, especially where independent technical evidence points to Russian filtering/throttling or where the narrative may have been pre-positioned before restrictions. Separate verified historical cases from the user's archived 2014 lead until original materials are supplied.

core_mechanism.name: TECHNICAL_BLAME_SHIFTING_OR_PREPOSITIONED_COVER_STORY
sequence: seed a technical explanation that blames the foreign platform/CDN/provider
later access to the platform degrades or is restricted
repeat the pre-seeded explanation as the apparent cause
reduce public attribution of the outage/restriction to domestic policy or filtering infrastructure
core_mechanism.strategic_value: If successful, the same actor can impose or benefit from access restrictions while preserving plausible deniability and redirecting user anger toward the external platform or the West.

confirmed_public_precedents.finding: Google services became unavailable to Rostelecom subscribers because of a software failure in Russian equipment analyzing IP addresses for the federal blocking registry. Similar late-March problems affected YouTube and other sites.
confirmed_public_precedents.interpretation: Demonstrates that access failures to Google/YouTube in Russia can originate in the domestic filtering layer rather than Google infrastructure.

confirmed_public_precedents.finding: Russian state/state-aligned media prominently framed YouTube/Google restrictions on RT as external platform blocking. In March 2014 Google itself said the RT channel suspension was a technical error; in July the dispute involved copyright/function restrictions.
confirmed_public_precedents.interpretation: Shows an established narrative habit of emphasizing foreign-platform restriction, but these specific 2014 events are not evidence that Russia secretly caused the restrictions. Preserve as context, not attribution proof.

confirmed_public_precedents.finding: Russian officials and Roskomnadzor publicly attributed YouTube performance degradation to Google's alleged failure to maintain Google Global Cache infrastructure after leaving Russia.

Independent traffic analysis and telecom-industry sources reported that the slowdown was targeted throttling by Russian authorities rather than a simultaneous failure of Google Global Cache equipment; authorities later notified providers of severe YouTube rate limits, according to industry reporting.
confirmed_public_precedents.interpretation: This is the clearest public precedent for technical blame-shifting: platform degradation was publicly blamed on Google infrastructure while independent evidence pointed to intentional domestic throttling.

user_2014_archive_lead.claim: The user reports archived early-2014 cases/accounts that allegedly pre-positioned a narrative that Google clusters were degrading and that Google/Western platforms, rather than Russian authorities, were responsible for YouTube/resource blocking.
not_yet_established: whether the materials predate specific later restrictions
whether the accounts were coordinated or state-linked
whether the wording explicitly references Google cluster/CDN degradation
whether the same accounts/narratives reappeared during later blocking events
user_2014_archive_lead.evidentiary_value_if_verified: VERY_HIGH_PREPOSITIONING_VALUE because a dated technical cover story published before the corresponding restriction would support intentional narrative preparation rather than post-hoc explanation.
required_preservation: archive.org or other independent snapshots where available
later posts reusing the same explanation during actual degradation/blocking

analytical_distinctions: A genuine Google outage is not Russian blame-shifting.
A real Google moderation action against RT is not evidence Russia caused the action.
A domestic filtering failure that breaks Google access is evidence of filtering-layer causation, not necessarily deception.
Blame-shifting requires a mismatch between public attribution and stronger technical evidence of domestic intervention.
Pre-positioning requires chronology: the cover narrative must demonstrably exist before or independently of the restriction it later explains.

relevance_to_current_outreach.FBI: HIGH if the 2014 archive shows coordinated fake personas/accounts pre-seeding technical blame narratives; relevant to foreign influence and deception tradecraft.
relevance_to_current_outreach.ODNI_FMIC: HIGH as a strategic deception pattern linking technical control and attribution manipulation.
relevance_to_current_outreach.STATE_CFIMI: HIGH as a foreign-information-manipulation tactic: engineer or exploit access degradation while assigning blame to the foreign platform/West.
relevance_to_current_outreach.META: MEDIUM only if the same accounts or coordinated platform behavior can be demonstrated; otherwise keep out of the platform-abuse complaint.
relevance_to_current_outreach.CISA: HOLD unless tied to measurable active network events; technical mismatch between claimed provider failure and path-localized filtering would be relevant after trigger.

best_current_claim: A documented 2024 Russian case shows the official attribution of YouTube degradation to Google Global Cache deterioration while independent traffic evidence pointed to intentional Russian throttling. This establishes technical blame-shifting as a real precedent. The user's reported 2014 archive may indicate an earlier pre-positioned version of the same tactic, but that chronology and attribution remain unverified until the original materials are preserved and examined.
